concerns.text: The plan performs Wilcoxon signed‑rank tests on F1‑scores using only **5 random seeds** (see “perform Wilcoxon signed‑rank tests on F1‑scores across the required 5 seeds for the seven prescribed comparisons”). With n=5 the smallest attainable two‑sided p‑value is ≈0.0625, which cannot meet the required Benjamini‑Hochberg adjusted FDR < 0.05 (SC‑003). Consequently the methodology cannot substantiate a claim of statistical significance.

Baseline models (Random Forest, XGBoost) are trained on hand‑crafted structural features, while the GCN leverages full graph topology. Differences in model capacity and input representation constitute a confound: any observed performance gap may be due to richer input rather than the intrinsic advantage of graph neural networks. The plan does not include a control that isolates the effect of graph structure (e.g., a non‑graph model using the same adjacency information as features).
